narration.text: Once, every person on earth spoke the same language. And they used it to build something that would make them famous.
And the whole earth was of one language, and of one speech.
They found a wide plain called Shinar and they had a plan. There was no stone in that land, so they made their own.
And they said one to another, Go to, let us make brick, and burn them throughly. And they had brick for stone, and slime had they for morter.
Fire, clay and black tar. Thousands of hands, one voice, one purpose. Day after day the walls climbed higher over the plain. And then the purpose turned.
And they said, Go to, let us build us a city and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven; and let us make us a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.
Do you see it? Not to honour God. To make a name for themselves. They were afraid of the very world God had told them to fill.
And the Lord came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men builded.
Came down. A tower meant to reach heaven, and God had to come down just to see it. From where He sits, their greatest work was very small.
And the Lord said, Behold, the people is one, and they have all one language; and this they begin to do:
God was not afraid of bricks. He saw what a proud and united people could become, and in mercy He stopped them before it was too late.
Go to, let us go down, and there confound their language, that they may not understand one another’s speech.
Imagine it. A man calls to his friend across the scaffold and hears only strange sounds. The brick falls from his hands. Both of them are afraid, and neither can say why.
So the Lord scattered them abroad from thence upon the face of all the earth: and they left off to build the city.

Families gathered their bundles and walked away in every direction. The tower stood unfinished on the empty plain, with the wind in its scaffolds. The one language that bound them together was gone, and so was their pride.
Therefore is the name of it called Babel; because the Lord did there confound the language of all the earth:
The builders wanted to make a name for themselves, and lost it. Soon after, God gives one man a name for free, and makes it great.
Would you rather build your own name, or receive one? Tell me below.
The full story is in the long video. Part thirteen tomorrow: God calls Abram.
